title: New Horizons passed about 12,500 km above Pluto
body: On 14 July 2015, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew within about 12,500 km of Pluto. It gathered close-up observations during a flyby and continued beyond the dwarf planet into the Kuiper Belt.
takeaway: A brief close pass can collect observations without needing the fuel required to stop and enter orbit.
visual: a small spacecraft passing above the bright heart-shaped region of Pluto

title: Kepler searched for planets by watching stars grow briefly dimmer
body: Launched in 2009, NASA's Kepler telescope watched a patch of sky to catch repeated dips in a star's light. A planet passing in front of its star blocks a little of that light for a short time.
takeaway: This method can find a planet even when the telescope never sees light from the planet itself.
source: NASA Science, How We Find and Characterize Exoplanets
visual: a tiny dark planet silhouetted against the disc of a bright star
